collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager wrongly told people a neighbor's stew made them sick: ask them to set it straight, or ask the cook what would help.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) told several people that (friend)'s fish stew made (subject.him/her) sick. It didn't: it turns out (subject) had eaten a bad clam earlier that day. But the story has spread, and nobody has touched (friend)'s stew since. (friend) has asked the elders for help.

choices.label: Ask (subject) to Set the Story Straight

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The elders ask (subject) to tell the people (subject.he/she) told that (subject.he/she) was wrong: no speech, no apology in front of everyone, just the facts. (subject) does it at the fire, briefly and clearly. Then, without being asked, (subject.he/she) holds out a bowl for (friend)'s stew. Others follow.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The elders ask (friend) what (friend.he/she) would like. (friend) thinks. "I'd like (subject.him/her) to try my stew again, and say honestly whether it's good." (subject) does. It's very good, and (subject.he/she) says so, plainly. Coming from (subject), it's the most convincing thing anyone could have said. The stew pot is empty by the end of the evening.
